Thanks, Aditya — reviewed the SOW and the requested $12k credit. High-level accounting guidance below: 

1) Treatment: For customer-facing promo credits tied to a future invoice (pilot/top-up discounts) we generally record as contra-revenue (GL 4205). Only record as marketing expense if the credit is strictly a third-party acquisition cost and not reducible from revenue. This appears to be a contra-revenue case.

2) ERP flow: Issue a credit memo in NetSuite referencing the original (or next) invoice number and apply as an invoice offset. Use AR adjustment type "Credit Memo - Promo" and tag with project code SKYL-PILOT.

3) Tax/VAT: If Skylark is US-based (Alice confirms), no VAT. Sales tax depends on jurisdiction and product nexus — please confirm Skylark's billing address. If non-US, we will need to include VAT reversal notes.

4) Approvals: Credits > $10,000 require manager + finance lead approval per policy. Marissa please confirm whether you can approve or if we need Marcus.

I'll prepare the draft credit memo template once approvals are confirmed.

-Laura
Laura Bennett

Thanks for the thorough notes. Approve the $12,000 credit memo as contra-revenue (GL 4205) and instruct AR to apply as an invoice offset in NetSuite with project code SKYL-PILOT. A few additional controls: 

- Require a short memo in the customer record describing business rationale (POC concession) and link to the SOW.
- Limit the credit memo expiry to 180 days from issuance.
- If sales tax jurisdiction later indicates taxable treatment, we'll reverse the memo and post the appropriate VAT/Tax entries.
